title: Oncogenic transformation by inhibitor-sensitive and -resistant EGFR mutants.
abstract: BackgroundSomatic mutations in the kinase domain of the epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase gene EGFR are common in lung adenocarcinoma.

The presence of mutations correlates with tumor sensitivity to the EGFR inhibitors erlotinib and gefitinib, but the transforming potential of specific mutations and their relationship to drug sensitivity have not been described.Methods and findingsHere, we demonstrate that EGFR active site mutants are oncogenic.

Mutant EGFR can transform both fibroblasts and lung epithelial cells in the absence of exogenous epidermal growth factor, as evidenced by anchorage-independent growth, focus formation, and tumor formation in immunocompromised mice.
Transformation is associated with constitutive autophosphorylation of EGFR, Shc phosphorylation, and STAT pathway activation.

Whereas transformation by most EGFR mutants confers on cells sensitivity to erlotinib and gefitinib, transformation by an exon 20 insertion makes cells resistant to these inhibitors but more sensitive to the irreversible inhibitor CL-387,785.ConclusionOncogenic transformation of cells by different EGFR mutants causes differential sensitivity to gefitinib and erlotinib.
Treatment of lung cancers harboring EGFR exon 20 insertions may therefore require the development of alternative kinase inhibition strategies.

body.section: Introduction
body.text: The human epidermal growth factor receptor gene product (EGFR), a member of the ErbB family of receptor tyrosine kinases, is an integral component of signaling in epithelial cell proliferation.

body.section: Introduction
body.text: Stimulation of the receptor with EGF or other cognate ligands induces receptor dimerization and autophosphorylation, providing docking sites for SH2-containing adaptor proteins that mediate the activation of intracellular signaling pathways [-].

body.section: Introduction
body.text: Consistent with a role in proliferative signaling, the oncogenic potential of EGFR variants with deletions in the extracellular domain, including the v-erbB oncogene of avian erythroblastosis virus and the vIII mutant found in human cancers, transforms vertebrate cells in the absence of exogenous EGF [-].

body.section: Introduction
body.text: In contrast, overexpression of the wild-type EGFR gene can transform NIH-3T3 cells only upon EGF addition [].

body.section: Introduction
body.text: Kinase activity is required for ligand-independent transformation by both types of EGFR extracellular domain deletion mutant [,].

body.section: Introduction
body.text: A series of novel EGFR kinase domain mutations observed in human lung adenocarcinomas has recently been described [-].

body.section: Introduction
body.text: These mutations arise in four exons: substitutions for G719 in the nucleotide-binding loop of exon 18, in-frame deletions within exon 19, in-frame insertions within exon 20, and substitutions for L858 or L861 in the activation loop in exon 21.

body.section: Introduction
body.text: Tumors from patients with clinical responses to the EGFR inhibitors gefitinib or erlotinib have been shown to contain EGFR deletion mutations or substitution mutations [,,,], but no exon 20 insertion mutations have been reported in this group of clinical responders.

body.section: Introduction
body.text: Although exon 20 mutations were not widely reported at first, recently five large-scale studies that sequenced EGFR exons 18 through 21 reported a total of 18 exon 20 insertions out of 350 EGFR mutations identified in 1,108 non-small-cell lung cancers [-].

body.section: Introduction
body.text: Patients who responded to gefitinib and subsequently relapsed were found to have T790M secondary mutations, also in exon 20 [,].

body.section: Introduction
body.text: Although gefitinib treatment and small interfering RNA experiments suggest that cells expressing mutant EGFR are dependent on EGFR function for survival [,,], the direct transforming potential of the mutations observed in lung adenocarcinoma has not been described.

body.section: Introduction
body.text: Here, we assess the ability of these EGFR kinase domain mutations to constitutively activate EGFR signaling and contribute to tumorigenesis in model cell culture systems.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: To assess the oncogenic potential of EGFR kinase domain mutants, tumor-derived mutations were introduced into the wild-type human EGFR cDNA by site-directed mutagenesis.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: The resulting wild-type and mutant EGFR cDNAs were then cloned into the pBabe-Puro retroviral vector and transferred into NIH-3T3 cells by retroviral infection.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: We initially examined two representative substitution mutations: G719S, observed in exon 18, and L858R, observed in exon 21 (Figure 1).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: The L858R and G719S mutants were able to transform NIH-3T3 cells to anchorage independence in the absence of exogenous EGF, as assayed by colony formation in soft agar (Figure 1A, top photographs).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: In contrast, as previously described [], wild-type EGFR transformed only upon EGF addition (Figure 1A, bottom photographs).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: The kinase-dead D837A mutant [], included as a negative control, failed to induce colony formation in the presence or absence of EGF.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: EGFR expression levels were approximately equal for each pooled stably-transfected cell population (Figure 1B).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: Clonal cell lines derived from the pooled stably-transfected cells expressing the mutant EGFR exhibited profound morphological alterations characterized by a fusiform, refractile phenotype (unpublished data).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: Levels of L858R EGFR expression necessary to achieve transformation in this model cell culture system were no higher than expression levels observed in the human lung adenocarcinoma cell line H3255 bearing the L858R mutation (Figure 1C).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: Transformation of NIH-3T3 cells by L858R or G719S EGFR was further assessed in two independent assays.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: Expression of the EGFR point mutants in NIH-3T3 cells caused loss of contact inhibition, resulting in focus formation on an unselected monolayer, whereas the wild-type and D837A kinase-inactive controls did not (Table 1).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: In addition, injection of clonal, transformed NIH-3T3 fibroblasts expressing L858R and G719S EGFR into immunocompromised mice led to the formation of tumors (Table 2).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: No tumor formation was observed upon injection of cells infected with vector, wild-type, and kinase-dead controls.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: Representative exon 19 deletion and exon 20 insertion mutations of EGFR were then assessed for transforming activity.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: Mutants L747_E749del, A750P [] and D770_N771insNPG (K.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: Naoki and M.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: M., unpublished data) were introduced into NIH-3T3 cells by retrovirus-mediated gene transfer as described above.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: Cells expressing the EGFR deletion and insertion mutants formed colonies in soft agar with a higher efficiency than that of cells expressing the missense mutants, comparable to the colony formation efficiency of cells expressing polyoma middle T antigen (Figure 1D).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: Expression of the deletion mutant was comparable to that of L858R EGFR, whereas expression of the insertion mutant was lower, as reflected in the EGFR expression levels of the clonal cell lines (Figure 2A and unpublished data).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: Cells expressing the L747_E749del A750P and D770_N771insNPG EGFR mutants also exhibited a greater degree of loss of contact inhibition than was observed in cells expressing the L858R or G719S EGFR mutants in a primary focus formation assay (unpublished data).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: To determine the ability of mutant EGFR to transform a more physiologically relevant cell type, retroviruses expressing the L858R and G719S mutant forms of EGFR were introduced into hTBE cells expressing the SV40 early region T antigens and the human telomerase catalytic subunit hTERT [].

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: We previously showed that such cells are fully transformed by the additional expression of oncogenic alleles of H- or K-RAS [].

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: Similarly, the expression of L858R and G719S mutant EGFR genes conferred enhanced anchorage-independent growth upon such hTBE cells, with colony numbers approximately 15-fold above the background level of microscopic colonies observed in hTBE cells expressing wild-type EGFR or a control vector (Figure 1E).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: The representative deletion and insertion mutants, L747_E749del A750P and D770_N771insNPG, formed colonies in soft agar with even greater efficiency, with the caveat that the deletion mutant is expressed at higher levels than the other mutants in this assay (Figure 1F).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: Similar to hTBE cells expressing H-RAS V12, expression of these EGFR mutants did not increase the rate of cell proliferation in defined medium (unpublished data).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Induces Oncogenic Transformation
body.text: Multiple tumor-derived mutants of EGFR therefore contribute to oncogenic transformation as shown by three different assays: anchorage-independent cell growth, focus formation, and in vivo tumor formation.

body.section: Mutant EGFR Proteins Are Constitutively Active
body.text: To determine whether transformation by mutant EGFR is associated with constitutive receptor activation in the absence of exogenous EGF, tyrosine autophosphorylation in the C-terminal tail of EGFR was examined by immunoblotting of cell lysates.

body.section: Mutant EGFR Proteins Are Constitutively Active
body.text: Constitutive tyrosine phosphorylation of the mutant EGFR molecules was observed at several C-terminal sites, including Y845, Y1068, and Y1173 (Figure 2A).

body.section: Mutant EGFR Proteins Are Constitutively Active
body.text: High-level phosphorylation of the insertion mutant at Y1045, the docking site for the Cbl E3 ubiquitin ligase [], is correlated with decreased abundance of this protein (Figure 2A), but whether the differential protein levels are a result of Cbl activity has not been confirmed.

body.section: Mutant EGFR Proteins Are Constitutively Active
body.text: The constitutive increase in EGFR activity appears to be ligand-independent, as a combination of neutralizing antibodies against EGF, TGFα, and EGFR failed to inhibit elevated basal levels of L858R autophosphorylation (Figure 2B).

body.section: Mutant EGFR Proteins Are Constitutively Active
body.text: However, tyrosine phosphorylation on the EGFR mutants could be further increased by EGF stimulation (Figure 2B), suggesting that the mutant EGFRs exhibit both ligand-independent and ligand-dependent activation, similar to that observed upon EGF stimulation of the L858R mutant H3255 lung adenocarcinoma cell line [].

body.section: Mutant EGFR Proteins Are Constitutively Active
body.text: Ligand-independent activation of EGFR with lung cancer-derived kinase domain mutations has not been observed by other groups working with transient transfection systems [,].

body.section: Mutant EGFR Proteins Are Constitutively Active
body.text: We too have failed to detect constitutive elevation of mutant receptor autophosphorylation when transiently expressed in NIH-3T3 and HeLa cells (unpublished data).

body.section: Mutant EGFR Proteins Are Constitutively Active
body.text: The reason for this phenotypic difference remains unclear.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Results in Activation of Shc, STAT3, and Akt
body.text: We next asked whether constitutive activation of mutant EGFR is associated with alterations in downstream signaling pathways.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Results in Activation of Shc, STAT3, and Akt
body.text: Because Y1173, a docking site for the adaptor protein Shc [], is constitutively phosphorylated on mutant EGFR (Figure 2A), we analyzed Shc-EGFR complex formation in cells expressing wild-type and mutant EGFR.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Results in Activation of Shc, STAT3, and Akt
body.text: Coimmunoprecipitation studies revealed a low level of constitutive Shc binding to the L858R EGFR, further augmented by EGF stimulation (Figure 3A), whereas Shc complexed with the wild-type EGFR only upon EGF stimulation.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Results in Activation of Shc, STAT3, and Akt
body.text: Immunoblotting of whole cell lysates with an antibody specific for tyrosine-phosphorylated Shc revealed constitutive phosphorylation on Shc in cells expressing the L858R EGFR, consistent with the known phosphorylation of EGFR-bound Shc []; in contrast, in cells expressing wild-type EGFR, Shc was phosphorylated only in response to EGF stimulation (Figure 3B).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Results in Activation of Shc, STAT3, and Akt
body.text: Similar to the situation with receptor autophosphorylation, constitutive phosphorylation of Shc in mutant EGFR-expressing cells has not been observed in transient expression systems [].

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Results in Activation of Shc, STAT3, and Akt
body.text: Consistent with previous reports on L858R mutant EGFR [], STAT signaling pathways are constitutively activated in the transformed NIH-3T3 cells.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Results in Activation of Shc, STAT3, and Akt
body.text: Immunoblotting with antibodies specific for phosphorylated Y705, the tyrosine responsible for STAT3 dimerization [], revealed constitutive phosphorylation in cells expressing the lung cancer-derived mutant EGFR but not wild-type EGFR (Figure 3C).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Results in Activation of Shc, STAT3, and Akt
body.text: Increased STAT3-dependent gene expression in cells expressing the mutant EGFRs was confirmed in a reporter assay (Figure 3D) using a STAT-dependent luciferase construct [].

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Results in Activation of Shc, STAT3, and Akt
body.text: Constitutive phosphorylation of mutant EGFR on Y1068 (see Figure 2A), the binding site for the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase interacting protein Gab1 [], indicated that signaling pathways downstream of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase might be constitutively activated as well.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Results in Activation of Shc, STAT3, and Akt
body.text: One such pathway is controlled by the serine/threonine kinase Akt, which is involved in promotion of cell survival.

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Results in Activation of Shc, STAT3, and Akt
body.text: Western blotting with anti-phospho-Akt confirmed that Akt is constitutively activated in cells expressing the mutant EGFR (Figure 3E).

body.section: Expression of Mutant EGFR Results in Activation of Shc, STAT3, and Akt
body.text: We therefore conclude that at least a subset of physiological EGFR signaling pathways is activated by stable expression of mutant EGFR.

body.section: Transformation by the Exon 20 Insertion Mutant Is Not Sensitive to Gefitinib or Erlotinib
body.text: Given the association between the presence of activating EGFR mutations and clinical responses to gefitinib or erlotinib in lung adenocarcinoma patients [,,,], we assessed the ability of these EGFR inhibitors to inhibit anchorage-independent growth of clonal NIH-3T3 cell lines expressing wild-type or mutant EGFR.

body.section: Transformation by the Exon 20 Insertion Mutant Is Not Sensitive to Gefitinib or Erlotinib
body.text: Consistent with the increased sensitivity to gefitinib and erlotinib of patient tumors harboring the missense mutations or exon 19 deletions, anchorage-independent growth of cells expressing L858R, G719S, or L747_E749del A750P was inhibited by 100 nM erlotinib (Figure 4A and 4B) or gefitinib (Figure 4B and unpublished data), although the G719S mutant may be somewhat more resistant to gefitinib (Figure 4A and unpublished data), consistent with other in vitro studies [].

body.section: Transformation by the Exon 20 Insertion Mutant Is Not Sensitive to Gefitinib or Erlotinib
body.text: In contrast, 1 μM erlotinib (Figure 4A) or gefitinib (unpublished data) did not inhibit anchorage-independent growth of EGF-treated cells overexpressing the wild-type EGFR.

body.section: Transformation by the Exon 20 Insertion Mutant Is Not Sensitive to Gefitinib or Erlotinib
body.text: Transformation by the D770_N771insNPG EGFR mutant was remarkably insensitive to gefitinib and erlotinib, as inhibition of colony growth in soft agar required exposure to 100-fold higher concentrations (>1 μM) of these agents than was required to inhibit colony formation by cells expressing the EGFR missense mutants or deletion mutant (Figure 4A).

body.section: Transformation by the Exon 20 Insertion Mutant Is Not Sensitive to Gefitinib or Erlotinib
body.text: In fact, no significant inhibition of anchorage-independent growth of cells expressing D770_N771insNPG EGFR was observed at 3 μM gefitinib or erlotinib (Figure 4B).

body.section: Transformation by the Exon 20 Insertion Mutant Is Not Sensitive to Gefitinib or Erlotinib
body.text: The concentrations of gefitinib or erlotinib necessary to reverse insertion mutant transformation are therefore higher than the achievable serum concentrations of gefitinib (0.5-1.0 μM) and possibly higher than the achievable serum concentrations of erlotinib (2.8-4.0 μM) [,].

body.section: Discussion
body.text: Treatment with the EGFR inhibitors gefitinib and erlotinib has led to dramatic responses in many lung cancer patients, predominantly for those cancers in which EGFR mutations can be detected.

body.section: Discussion
body.text: However, there has been a subset of lung cancer patients with these mutations who do not respond to the EGFR inhibitors in current clinical use.

body.section: Discussion
body.text: By demonstrating that lung-cancer derived kinase domain mutants of EGFR are constitutively activated and that they can transform cultured mammalian cells, we have provided an in vitro system with which to study EGFR-dependent oncogenesis in a genetically homogeneous background.

body.section: Discussion
body.text: Although the anchorage-independent growth assay measures only one of many phenotypes of transformation and does not, for example, recapitulate tumor microenvironment or account for the influence of the immune system on tumor formation, this system will be useful for dissecting inhibitor response and downstream signaling pathways, particularly for those mutants not found in existing cancer-derived cell lines.

body.section: Discussion
body.text: Using the NIH-3T3 transformation system, we have found that transformation by an exon 20 insertion mutant is resistant to inhibition by gefitinib and erlotinib.

body.section: Discussion
body.text: Strikingly, transformation by this EGFR exon 20 insertion mutant is more sensitive to treatment with an irreversible inhibitor, CL-387,785.

body.section: Discussion
body.text: This compound was previously found to be active against EGFR containing the exon 20 point mutation T790M, associated with resistance to gefitinib and erlotinib [].

body.section: Discussion
body.text: These results indicate a need for the use of novel EGFR inhibitors in primary treatment of lung cancers harboring the exon 20 insertion mutations.

body.section: Discussion
body.text: Furthermore, the distinct inhibitor sensitivity of various EGFR mutants argues that therapies may need to be targeted against specific mutant forms of a protein, whereas generalized inhibition of a particular oncogenic target may not be sufficient.

body.section: Background
body.text: While lung cancer is still one of the deadliest cancers, a new class of drugs called epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) inhibitors have shown promising results in some patients.

body.section: Background
body.text: As the name suggests, these drugs inhibit a protein called EGFR, which is altered in a subset of lung cancers.

body.section: What Did the Researchers Do and Find?
body.text: The aim of this study was to understand in more detail what role the different EGFR alterations played in the tumor and which ones made the tumor responsive to EGFR inhibitor treatment.

body.section: What Did the Researchers Do and Find?
body.text: First, the researchers introduced different altered EGFR versions into human cells and studied their behavior.

body.section: What Did the Researchers Do and Find?
body.text: The EGFR protein, which can stimulate cell growth, is normally tightly regulated and active only when a cell receives a signal from its neighbors.

body.section: What Did the Researchers Do and Find?
body.text: However, the alterations made the EGFR protein always active, regardless of a stimulating signal, and caused them to “grow out of control.” They then treated the cells expressing the various alterations with different EGFR inhibitor drugs and showed that the specific alteration determined whether cell growth could be stopped by a specific drug.

body.section: What Do the Results Mean for Patients?
body.text: EGFR inhibitors are still considered to be experimental treatment.

body.section: What Do the Results Mean for Patients?
body.text: Researchers are making progress in understanding how genetic alterations in EGFR cause abnormal growth in some lung cancers and also which specific alterations cause the tumor to be responsive to a particular drug.

body.section: What Do the Results Mean for Patients?
body.text: The goal is to match the tumor and the drug to maximize anti-tumor response and avoid giving a drug that doesn't work with a particular tumor.
